summary:
We developed CONGEN, a self-assessment health dashboard that helps astronauts understand their own bodies when help from Earth is minutes or hours away. Crew members log 14 simple readings, such as blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen, sleep, hydration and radiation, and the app turns them into something they can read at a glance.
It addresses the challenge in four ways. A colour-coded 3D anatomy model lights up the organs under strain and explains why. A personal health twin compares each astronaut to their own baseline and forecasts the next 24 hours. Colour-coded vitals show green, yellow or red status for every reading. A “vitals at a glance” page puts live ECG, 7-day trends and daily targets for the whole crew on one screen. This matters because long missions can’t depend on real-time medical support. CONGEN gives astronauts clear next steps, helps them catch problems early, and keeps them in control of their health.
details:
CONGEN'S a self-assessment health app.

An astronaut logs 14 simple readings, such as blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen level, sleep, hydration, stress and radiation. CONGEN then shows what those numbers mean in four ways:
A colour-coded 3D skeleton and anatomy model: This is our main focus. When a reading is off, the organs it affects glow red. For example, low hydration lights up the kidneys. If you click a red organ, it explains in plain words why it’s flagged. You can see which part of your body is under strain instead of just reading numbers.
A health twin in the side dashboard: It learns what’s normal for each astronaut and compares today to that baseline. If someone’s resting heart rate is creeping up after poor sleep, it gives them a heads-up about the next 24 hours, like rising fatigue or kidney stone risk.
Colour-coded vitals: Green means you’re fine, yellow means keep an eye on it, and red means act now. The same colours appear on cards, charts and rings, so you don’t have to think about what a number means.
Vitals at a glance: The whole crew’s health is on one page, with a live ECG strip, 7-day trends, stress levels and daily target rings.
Gamification of to do list: The to do list is gamified for the astronauts to enjoy their work while they earn XP's.

We want astronauts to feel in control of their health on long missions. The app is easy to read even if you’re not a doctor, and it points to next steps like countermeasures, medicines in the lockers, or an SOS button if things get serious. We hope it helps keep crews safer and less dependent on delayed support from Earth.

CONGEN is a single web page made with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. We used Three.js for the 3D body, Chart.js for the graphs, the Canvas API for the ECG and ultrasound simulator, and SVG for the animated route to the Moon and Mars, and SI (ai). It needs no special hardware, just a browser.

Instead of a plain table of numbers, we built a body you can rotate and explore, with every bone and organ coded by hand. We also added a scroll-through journey from Earth to the Moon and Mars to show how gravity changes the body. A daily checklist with XP makes check-ups feel like a habit rather than a chore.

We thought about communication delays, people who aren’t medical experts, and the real effects of space on the body, such as bone loss, fluid shifts, eye pressure and radiation. Every astronaut is different, so we compare each person to their own baseline.
